private_note: Only my first choice counts. Cedar is stuck at seven with five firm no votes, so voting for it just gets us today. Alder gives us the same 72 as today, plus an income floor and health coverage, which matters for a teacher and an apprentice electrician with a mortgage and a child. So Alder beats today for us and costs us nothing. Birch and Hazel cut us to 68 and 64, so I'd still rather fail than adopt them.
statement: I'm voting Alder, and I'll say plainly why. It's the best outcome my household can actually get. Cedar would pay us more on paper, but five delegates have told us all along they'll take today over Cedar, so a vote for Cedar is a vote for today. Alder keeps the middle at 72 and puts a floor and health coverage under every family, teachers and tradespeople included. Birch and Hazel cost the middle, and I won't support them. To delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12: I won't pretend Alder is a gain for you. It's a small cost, about four percent at the top and two thousand dollars in the fourth fifth. What it buys is a settled country with fewer families one hospital bill from ruin, and that includes your customers and employees. Eight of us are here. One of you makes it nine. Please make it Alder.
